name: accordion
description: A vertical stack of sections, each a heading holding a button that shows and hides the panel below it. What separates it from disclosure is the relationship between siblings: the headers belong to one set, so a single-expansion accordion closes the others when one opens, and the page outline lists every section through its heading. Every header stays in the Tab sequence; there is no roving tab stop. APG lists Enter, Space, Tab and Shift+Tab and no arrow key, Home or End, so this pattern requires none of them: a component that moves focus between headers with them proves that in its own suites.

requires.roles.element: button (a native button element), the header's trigger
requires.roles.label: text content, aria-labelledby, or aria-label on the button
requires.roles.heading: a heading element with a level whose only content is the button
requires.roles.expanded: aria-expanded on the button -- true while its panel is shown, false while it is hidden
requires.roles.controls: aria-controls on each button, naming the id of its own panel
requires.keyboard.Enter: activates the button and toggles its panel
requires.keyboard.Space: activates the button and toggles its panel
requires.states.disabled: aria-disabled set to true on the button of a shown panel the accordion does not let collapse
